stem: Which inequality shows all possible values of $t$?
stimulus: A weaver's cloth has a thread count $t$ of at least 40 threads per inch but no more than 60 threads per inch.
explanation: 'At least 40' means $t \ge 40$, so 40 is included. 'No more than 60' means $t \le 60$, so 60 is included too. Put the lower bound on the left: $40 \le t \le 60$. This is the step behind every SAT question that describes a quantity between a low and a high value. Before you look at any numbers, turn each phrase into its symbol.

A.why: You read both phrases as strict. 'At least' and 'no more than' both include their endpoint, so a cloth with exactly 40 or exactly 60 threads per inch counts.

C.why: You treated 'no more than 60' as 'less than 60'. 'No more than' allows 60 itself, so that end needs $\le$.

D.why: You put the bounds the wrong way round. No number is at least 60 and at most 40 at the same time. The smaller value, the minimum, goes on the left.

stem: Which inequality shows all possible values of $w$?
stimulus: The wingspan $w$, in centimeters, of a species of warbler is more than 18 but less than 24.
explanation: 'More than 18' is strict, $w > 18$, and 'less than 24' is strict, $w < 24$. Neither endpoint is included, so the answer is $18 < w < 24$. On between-two-values questions, the strictness at each end is often the only difference between the choices. Practising this step is how you learn to see it.

A.why: You used $\le$ at both ends. 'More than' and 'less than' are strict, so a wingspan of exactly 18 or exactly 24 cm is not included.

B.why: You swapped the bounds. No number is both greater than 24 and less than 18. The lower bound, 18, belongs on the left.

D.why: You got the lower end right but read 'less than 24' as 'no more than 24'. Both ends here are strict.

stem: Which of the following tempos is in this range?
stimulus: A composer marks a movement to be played at a tempo of at least 96 beats per minute but less than 120 beats per minute.
explanation: Write the range as $96 \le b < 120$. 'At least 96' includes 96, so 96 meets both conditions: it is at least 96, and it is less than 120. Some SAT range questions ask you to check numbers against a range instead of choosing an inequality. Write the double inequality first, then test each choice against both ends.

A.why: 92 is less than 120, but it is below the minimum of 96. A value has to satisfy both ends of the range.

C.why: You read 'less than 120' as 'no more than 120'. The upper bound is strict, so 120 itself is not in the range.

D.why: 126 is at least 96, but it goes past the upper limit. You checked only the lower bound.

stem: Which inequality shows all possible values of $T$?
stimulus: On one winter day, the air temperature $T$, in degrees Celsius, at a weather station had a minimum of $-4$ and a maximum of $7$.
explanation: A minimum of $-4$ means $T \ge -4$, and a maximum of 7 means $T \le 7$. Both endpoints were actually reached, so both are included: $-4 \le T \le 7$. Many SAT questions give a range using 'minimum' and 'maximum'. The minimum always becomes the left-hand bound with $\le$.

A.why: You attached the negative sign to the wrong number. The minimum is $-4$ and the maximum is 7, not $-7$ and 4.

B.why: You made both ends strict. A minimum and a maximum are values the temperature actually reached, so both endpoints are included.

C.why: You swapped the minimum and the maximum. No temperature is both at least 7 and at most $-4$. The minimum goes on the left.
